citation: Yeung CY, Men VY, Guo Y, Yip PSF. Spatial–temporal analysis of suicide clusters for suicide prevention in Hong Kong: a territory-wide study using 2014–2018 Hong Kong Coroner’s Court reports. The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific. 2023;39:100820. doi:10.1016/j.lanwpc.2023.100820.
title: Spatial–temporal analysis of suicide clusters for suicide prevention in Hong Kong: a territory-wide study using 2014–2018 Hong Kong Coroner’s Court reports
abstract: Territory-wide retrospective spatial-temporal analysis of Hong Kong suicide deaths to identify high-risk clusters by method and compare characteristics inside and outside identified clusters.
setting: Hong Kong small tertiary planning units
uncertainty: Cluster-level relative risks describe ecological space-time concentrations and are not individual risk estimates.
Community-level characteristics were based on area-level data and are vulnerable to ecological inference limitations.
methods: bivariate comparison of cases and spatial units inside versus outside clusters

evidence_claims.statement: Among 4,672 suicide deaths recorded in Hong Kong from 2014 to 2018, the study identified statistically significant spatial-temporal clusters for jumping and charcoal burning, but not for hanging.

provenance.locator: Article pp. 1 and 4, Summary Findings and Results
provenance.source_span: The paper reports 4,672 cases and identifies clusters for jumping and charcoal burning, with no significant hanging cluster.

evidence_claims.statement: For residence-based clusters, reported relative risks were 1.47 for overall suicide, 1.89 for jumping and 4.34 for charcoal burning during the identified cluster periods.

provenance.source_span: Table 1 reports the cluster periods, case counts, population sizes, relative risks and p-values.

evidence_claims.statement: Most overall-suicide and jumping clusters were located in spatial units that were more socially disadvantaged than units outside the clusters.

provenance.source_span: The authors report greater social disadvantage in most overall and jumping cluster areas relative to outside areas.

limitations: Ecological/area-level analysis cannot be used to infer an individual’s suicide probability.
Cluster detection depends on spatial-unit definitions, time windows and available location data.
Community-level characteristics do not establish individual-level causal mechanisms.
applicability: Supports population-level surveillance, area prioritization and community prevention planning.
Useful for targeting further investigation and services, not for individual prediction.
safety_boundaries: Never convert area-level cluster relative risk into an individual suicide-risk percentage.
Do not label residents within a cluster as high-risk individuals solely on the basis of geography.
